paper_metadata.title: Advancing Stock Price Prediction and Algorithmic Trading: Quantum Machine Learning for High-Frequency Optimization

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical stock price prediction and HFT optimization using QSVM, QNN, and QA on historical market data, evaluated for execution speed, prediction accuracy, and risk management across multiple sample sizes.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Hybrid Trading Predictor (QHTP) / QML-based HFT optimization framework

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Historical price/feature windows are normalized and embedded; classical sequence features are combined with market microstructure features and mapped into a parameterized quantum circuit via AngleMap.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Predict next-step stock price and trading signal (BUY/SELL/HOLD) while maximizing execution speed and risk management efficiency.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Trading thresholds delta_up and delta_down are used to generate buy/sell/hold signals; stop-loss, hedging, and automated controls are applied in the trading pipeline.

problem_instance.description: Stock price prediction and high-frequency trading on historical market data with technical indicators and market microstructure features.

dataset_specification.description: Historical stock price data with Open, High, Low, Close, Adjusted Close, and Volume for many companies over several years; preprocessing included forward-filling missing values, Z-score outlier removal, Moving Average (MA) and Relative Strength Index (RSI) feature engineering, Min-Max scaling for price-related features, log scaling for volume, and 80/20 train-test split.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Normalization, embedding, multi-head attention, residual connections, layer normalization, feed-forward block, angle mapping, quantum feature encoding.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Dense layer combines classical and quantum outputs to produce predicted price and trading signal.

speedup_claims.conditions: on the reported stock-market dataset and Qiskit simulator / IBM hardware validation
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper reports percentage improvement/efficiency rather than absolute latency; exact baseline time not provided.

experiments.description: QSVM-based stock price prediction and HFT optimization evaluated on historical market data and compared against QA, PCA, and HFT baselines across sample sizes.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: The paper states that QSVM uses quantum feature maps to encode data into quantum states; exact qubit mapping is not specified.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary classification of stock price movement (up/down) and optimization of trade execution speed.

problem_instance.description: Binary stock trend classification and HFT execution-speed evaluation on market data.

dataset_specification.description: Same dataset and preprocessing as the main experiment; evaluated over sample sizes 20, 40, 60, 80, and 100.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Forward-filling missing values, Z-score outlier removal, MA/RSI feature engineering, Min-Max scaling, log scaling, train-test split.

speedup_claims.conditions: reported on the Kaggle stock-market dataset with sample sizes 20, 40, 60, 80, 100
speedup_claims.caveats: No absolute runtime or latency values reported.

experiments.description: QNN-based stock price prediction and HFT optimization evaluated on historical market data and compared against classical baselines and other quantum methods.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical features are concatenated and mapped into a parameterized quantum circuit; the QNN applies entanglement and parameterized rotations.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Predict next stock price and improve execution speed/risk management in HFT.

problem_instance.description: Stock price forecasting and HFT decision support using market history and microstructure features.

dataset_specification.description: Same dataset and preprocessing as the main experiment; evaluated over sample sizes 20, 40, 60, 80, and 100.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Normalization, embedding, attention-based feature extraction, and angle mapping into the quantum circuit.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Dense layer combines classical and quantum outputs.

speedup_claims.conditions: same stock-market dataset; hybrid quantum-classical QNN pipeline
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states a 5% accuracy gain over SVM and LSTM, but does not provide a full per-model table for QNN alone.

experiments.description: Quantum annealing-based stock price prediction / feature selection and HFT optimization compared against QSVM, PCA, and the hybrid framework.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: The paper describes QA as being used for dimensionality reduction and feature selection, but does not provide an explicit binary-variable mapping or QUBO formulation.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Feature selection / dimensionality reduction for stock prediction and HFT optimization.

problem_instance.description: Stock prediction feature-selection / dimensionality-reduction task on the same market dataset.

dataset_specification.description: Same dataset and preprocessing as the main experiment; evaluated over sample sizes 20, 40, 60, 80, and 100.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Feature engineering and preprocessing as described for the main pipeline.

speedup_claims.conditions: reported for QA in the comparison table
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not clearly specify the exact baseline for the 57.8% figure in the table context.

experiments.description: Quantum simulator and IBM quantum hardware validation of the proposed QML-HFT framework, including runs on IBM Falcon 5 and IBM Eagle 16 processors.

algorithm.variant: Hybrid quantum-classical validation on simulator and real IBM QPUs

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same hybrid QML pipeline as the main experiment; quantum circuits were simulated and then executed on IBM hardware.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Validate execution speed, prediction accuracy, and computational economy under simulator and real-device conditions.

problem_instance.description: Validation of the QML-HFT framework on simulator and real quantum processors using the same stock-market prediction task.

dataset_specification.description: Same dataset and preprocessing as the main experiment; validation performed on simulator and IBM QPUs.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Same preprocessing pipeline as the main experiment.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Performance measured by execution speed, prediction accuracy, and computational economy.

speedup_claims.conditions: validation on IBM Falcon 5 and IBM Eagle 16 processors and Qiskit simulator
speedup_claims.caveats: Hardware noise, error rate, and finite coherence times are noted as limitations; no absolute runtime values reported.
